meaning: Plausible in-vivo adult Drosophila spike-rate ranges (Hz, population mean per cell over the window). spontaneous_hz applies to baseline windows, driven_hz to stimulus windows. A bound is a sanity range, not a target. verified:true means both ends of both intervals rest on values read from the cited sources (or are wider than every read value by the stated margin); anything recalled, inferred, or read only from figure axes stays verified:false.

ORN.basis: spontaneous: Hallem 2006 empty-neuron SFR 1-47 Hz for 24 Ors (DoOR.data), Hallem 2006 text 'receptors with spontaneous firing rates of <5 spikes/s (Or9a, Or22a, Or43b, Or47a, and Or59b)'; Kazama & Wilson 2008 'ORNs fire spontaneously at about 7 spikes/s' (VM2). driven: Hallem 2006 '69 ... 3%, resulted in very strong responses of >=200 spikes/s' (500 ms window, spontaneous subtracted, 1e-2 dilution); Kazama & Wilson 2008 'odors can easily trigger sustained ORN firing rates well above 200 spikes/s'; 300 Hz ceiling = 'the maximum ORN firing rate (~300 spikes/s)' in Wilson 2013 (review, secondary for Hallem 2006).

PN.basis: spontaneous VERIFIED: Turner, Bazhenov & Laurent 2008 Fig. 3F legend 'spontaneous spike rates in PNs (4.6 +/- 4.2 s^-1, n = 37 PNs)'; 20 Hz upper end is mean + ~3.7 SD. driven UNVERIFIED at the ceiling: Kazama & Wilson 2008 Discussion 'can evoke much stronger responses in postsynaptic PNs (>100 spikes/s)' (500 ms odour window) supports >100 Hz; no read source gives a PN maximum, so the 250 Hz ceiling is declared, not read. Wilson 2004 and Bhandawat 2007 could not be read.

KC.basis: spontaneous: Turner 2008 p.736 'very low spontaneous firing (0.1 +/- 0.4 spike/s)'. driven: Turner 2008 'a given odor evoked a spiking response in only 6 +/- 5% of the cells' (n = 71), responders fire 'alpha'/beta' 4.9 +/- 3.0 spikes ... alpha/beta 2.2 +/- 1.2' in the 0-2 s window; Murthy, Fiete & Laurent 2008: up to 49% of GFP- KCs respond under a >=1-spike criterion, 'with few spikes'. Even if every KC fired like an alpha'/beta' responder (4.9 spikes / 2 s = 2.45 Hz) the population mean would be ~2.5 Hz; the 5 Hz ceiling is twice that. Changed from v1 (20 Hz), which no source supported.

MBON.basis: spontaneous UNVERIFIED: no in-vivo MBON spontaneous rate found in Hige et al. 2015a/b (both subtract baseline without reporting it); an ex-vivo value (MBON-alpha3 12.1 Hz, n = 5, eLife 2022 77578) is not in vivo and is not used. driven (partly read): Hige et al. 2015 Neuron, MBON-gamma1pedc>alpha/beta OCT response '118 +/- 8.3 spikes' (0-1.4 s, spontaneous subtracted, n = 7), i.e. ~84 Hz above baseline; the 150 Hz ceiling is declared, not read.

DNa02.basis: UNVERIFIED: no absolute DNa02 rate appears in the text of Rayshubskiy et al. 2025 (rates in figures only) or Yang et al. 2024 Cell. Read: stride-locked modulation 'only about 15 spikes/sec' (Yang 2024, bioRxiv 2023.10.15.562426); DNa02 'hyperpolarizes during immobility' (Rayshubskiy Fig. 6). Figure axis limits in Rayshubskiy (e.g. Fig. 6D mean rate 0-120 spikes/s, Fig. 3C L-R difference -100..100) hint that the 100 Hz driven ceiling may be too tight; axis limits are not measurements, so the v1 values are kept.

GF.basis: UNVERIFIED (no measured rate exists in the sources read): the GF is quiet at rest (recordings kept only with resting potential below -55 mV, Ache 2019; below -50 mV, Jang 2023) and 'looming stimuli generate GF spikes in only a small subset of tethered flies' (von Reyn 2017); von Reyn 2014 Supp. Fig. 5 shows spiking in 10 flies and subthreshold responses in 33. 0-1 Hz spontaneous is an inference from these, not a read value.

LC_looming.basis: UNVERIFIED and currently unverifiable: every study read (von Reyn 2017, Ache 2019, Klapoetke 2017, Morimoto 2020) measured LC4/LPLC2 by calcium imaging or via GF subthreshold responses; no LC4 or LPLC2 firing rate in Hz was found. This bound is a modelling assumption.

LPTC.cell_types: HS (HSN, HSE, HSS); the optomotor spec checks HS only
LPTC.basis: UNVERIFIED: HS cells respond with graded potentials; Fujiwara et al. 2017 call them non-spiking during walking; Joesch 2008 (VS) reports graded responses 'superimposed by small action potentials of irregular amplitude'. Schnell et al. 2010 recorded HSN, HSE and HSS (not H2, as v1 implied) and only its abstract was readable. No HS spike rate in Hz was found. The LIF proxy can only spike, so this bound tests that it does not spike at high rates; the numbers are declared.

brain_mean.basis: DESIGN CHOICE, not a literature value: excludes the v1 runaway (~6 Hz mean, 1e6 spikes/s). Shiu 2024 used 0 Hz baselines and warns absolute rates are unreliable.

brain_max_single_neuron.basis: DESIGN CHOICE: no neuron sustained above 300 Hz over a window, well below the 1/t_ref ~ 450 Hz refractory ceiling where LIF output saturates.
